svg.title: Stable rank and memory capacity of 3901 human connectomes across the lifespan
svg.desc: Three scatter plots of 3901 connectomes from nine cohorts: stable rank against age, memory capacity against stable rank (Pearson r = 0.95 with the logarithm of the stable rank) and memory capacity against age (r = -0.72 up to 32 years and 0.44 after).

g.text: Each point is one of 3,901 structural connectomes (ages 0–90, nine cohorts), used as the fixed recurrent layer of the same echo-state network.
Its stable rank rs = ‖W‖F2 / ρ(W)2 is read from the weights; its memory capacity MC is measured as in the figure above.
Memory follows the stable rank: MC rises with rs with diminishing returns, close to a straight line in log rs (r = 0.95).
Summed over the network, the leading term of the walk expansion is the stable rank: Σi si2Yi = ρ(W)2 rs.
Across the lifespan the stable rank falls through development, reaches its minimum in the early thirties and rises again through aging.
Memory capacity follows the same course. Before adulthood, the trajectory compares different cohorts.
